 SubjectiveEuronews, carried by Ekkow—Russian strikes kill seven in Ukraine as Kyiv hits three refineriesRussia launched scores of drones at energy and civilian targets across Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, killing at least seven people in six regions, authorities said. The attack involved 112 Shahed, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, of which 88 were shot down or neutralised, Ukraine’s air force said. One person was killed in Bila Tserkva in Kyiv region, where the strike damaged critical infrastructure, an Epicentr shopping centre and a Nova Poshta postal branch, local authorities said. One person was killed and seven injured in Kharkiv region after a strike hit a minibus on a highway, regional governor Oleh Synehubov said. Two people aged 76 and 69 were killed and another wounded in Sumy region. Two people were killed in Odesa region on Tuesday evening—a 41-year-old and a 17-year-old—and one person was killed and three wounded in Zhytomyr region. Casualties were also reported in Chernihiv and Donetsk regions. Russian forces struck a Naftogaz gas production facility in the Poltava region, causing a fire and a suspension of operations, and a DTEK thermal power plant, causing serious damage and forcing it to stop generating electricity. More than 9,000 customers were left without electricity in Odesa region following Tuesday evening’s attacks. Ukrainian drones simultaneously struck three Russian oil refineries overnight, hitting plants in Samara and Rostov regions, according to Ukrainian monitoring sources. Two refineries in Samara region—the Kuibyshev and Syzran plants, both part of Rosneft—were struck, with fires breaking out at both facilities. Regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed the attack but did not name the facilities, saying one person was killed, power had been cut in several districts and a number of schools would operate on an adjusted schedule. Regional authorities said 145 drones were shot down over the Samara region. The third refinery struck overnight was the Novoshakhtinsk plant in Rostov region; its governor confirmed a combined strike of more than 50 drones and missiles lasting six hours before the plant suspended operations. Ukraine’s General Staff also reported overnight strikes on the Savasleyka airbase in Nizhny Novgorod region, saying three MiG-31 and two Su-34 aircraft were damaged.

 SubjectiveEuropeSays, carrying Ukrinform—Air defenses down 88 of 112 Russian drones targeting Ukraine overnightRussian forces attacked Ukraine with 112 attack drones overnight on the night of November 24-25. According to Ukrinform, the Ukrainian Air Force Command reported this on Telegram. ‘As of 08:00, air defenses had shot down or suppressed 88 enemy UAVs, including Shahed-type UAVs (47 of them jet-powered), Gerberas and other types of drones. Hits by enemy aerial weapons were recorded at 18 locations, while debris from downed drones fell at 13 locations,’ the statement said. According to the report, starting at 18:00 on November 24, Russian forces attacked Ukraine with 112 strike drones, including Shahed-type drones (66 of them jet-powered), Gerberas and Parodiya-type decoy drones, launched from Oryol, Millerovo, Kursk, Shatalovo and Primorsko-Akhtarsk in Russia, as well as the temporarily occupied parts of the Donetsk region and Crimea (Hvardiiske). The air attack was repelled by Ukrainian aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups. The attack is ongoing, with several enemy UAVs still in Ukrainian airspace.

 SubjectiveThe Gaze—Russia’s Rosneft Hit at Two Refineries in Overnight Ukrainian Drone AttackTwo major oil refineries operated by Rosneft caught fire in Russia’s Samara region following an overnight Ukrainian drone attack on November 25. The strikes hit the Syzran and Kuibyshev refineries, both part of Rosneft’s Samara refining group, which processes millions of tonnes of crude oil annually. Open-source analysts identified the Syzran refinery as one of the sites affected by the fires. A separate assessment placed the apparent impact area near several key processing facilities, including the ELOU-AVT-6 primary crude distillation unit, the PGI-DIG/280 installation and the 43-102 catalytic cracking unit. Fires were also reported in other sections of the refinery. The Kuibyshev refinery has an annual processing capacity of approximately 7 million tonnes. Both refineries have belonged to Rosneft’s Samara refining group since 2007. The full extent of the damage caused by the November 25 strikes has yet to be established.

 SubjectiveDefenceMENA—Ukraine Says Its Sea Drones Sank Russian Corvette Merkury in BenghaziUkraine says seven of its naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi naval base on 22 November and hit the cargo ship Angara off the city. Moscow has not confirmed the loss. Satellite imagery shows the corvette capsized alongside the quay. Two members of the eastern-based Libyan National Army’s naval forces died on 24 November of wounds sustained in the attack on the Benghazi naval base, the LNA General Command said, in the account’s update of 25 November 2026. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said on 24 November that the strikes were an exercise of Ukraine’s right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter and that Russian warships, cargo ships carrying military equipment and shadow-fleet tankers were legitimate targets. Russia’s Defence Ministry had still not commented on the Merkury by the time of this update.
